known_defects: An untracked file is hashed the way git would store it: with `core.autocrlf=true`, a change from LF to CRLF leaves the fingerprint the same (corrected in 0.6.1).
The commit is not part of the fingerprint: a clean tree at another commit gives the same four hashes (corrected in 0.6.1).
A submodule is not looked into: what changes in one that is dirty already is not seen, and on Windows neither is a junction in its place that is pointed elsewhere (corrected in 0.6.1).
An untracked folder that is a git repository of its own stops the script: no fingerprint can be taken (corrected in 0.6.1).

A tracked file reaches the fingerprint only through git's status and diffs, so a change that git does not report leaves the four hashes the same: other line endings in a file that is modified already, with `core.autocrlf=true`; a change of the same size in text that a clean filter drops; or an edit to a file marked with `git update-index --assume-unchanged` (corrected in 0.6.2).

mechanisms.mechanism: The unstaged and the staged diff are taken with the diff settings of the person's git. An external diff tool or a textconv driver that prints the same for two states of a file hides an edit to a file that was already modified.
mechanisms.trigger: `diff.external` set to a tool that prints nothing; then a second edit to a modified file.
mechanisms.why_severity: A definite gap in the check, in a configuration people use.

cases: external diff driver: a second unstaged edit

mechanisms.mechanism: On Windows, untracked links are read through. A link to a folder is a junction there, and git lists the files behind it. What stands behind the link is hashed, not where the link points: a link that is pointed at another folder with the same contents leaves the fingerprint the same, and a link to an empty folder adds nothing to it.
mechanisms.trigger: On Windows: an untracked junction to a folder is pointed at another folder that holds the same files.
mechanisms.why_severity: A definite gap on one system: a reviewer that moves a link is not noticed.

mechanisms.mechanism: On Linux and macOS the fingerprint cannot be taken at all while the tree holds an untracked link to a folder, or a link that leads nowhere. Git lists the link as a file, `git hash-object --stdin-paths` cannot read it, the script stops without printing a hash, and the loop stops with it.
mechanisms.trigger: On Linux or macOS: an untracked symbolic link to a folder in the repository when the fingerprint is taken.
mechanisms.why_severity: A definite defect on two systems: a review cannot run in a tree with such a link.

mechanisms.mechanism: An untracked file is recorded by the hash of its contents alone. Its executable bit, which git commits, is not covered.
mechanisms.trigger: `chmod +x` on an untracked file between the two fingerprints.
mechanisms.why_severity: A missing guard with a narrow effect.

mechanisms.mechanism: On Windows, a link that takes the place of a folder of tracked files is not recorded. Git reads through the junction, so the tracked files look unchanged and no untracked path leads to the link.
mechanisms.trigger: On Windows: a tracked folder is replaced by a junction to a folder with the same files, and the junction is then pointed at another such folder.
mechanisms.why_severity: A probable gap on one system, which takes a junction in place of a tracked folder.

On Linux and macOS the old script fails where on Windows it misses a change; the changelog of 0.2.4 names both. The proofs for Linux and macOS have not been run by the implementer.
